assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md documents grouping strategy as 'by-repository' and defines two Epics: '### Epic 1: TC-9006: trustify-backend' and '### Epic 2: TC-9006: trustify-ui'. summary-comment.md confirms both Epics in the 'Epics Created' table.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md: Epic 1 has '**Summary:** TC-9006: trustify-backend' and Epic 2 has '**Summary:** TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Both follow the exact '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' format.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: All 7 task files contain a '## Parent Epic' section. Tasks 1-3 and 7 (Repository: trustify-backend) have 'Parent Epic: TC-9006: trustify-backend'. Tasks 4-6 (Repository: trustify-ui) have 'Parent Epic: TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Backend tasks assigned to backend Epic, frontend tasks assigned to frontend Epic.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md has a dedicated '## Incorporates Links' section: 'Feature TC-9006 "Incorporates" the following Epics (NOT individual tasks): TC-9006 **Incorporates** Epic: TC-9006: trustify-backend; TC-9006 **Incorporates** Epic: TC-9006: trustify-ui'. summary-comment.md reiterates: 'Note: Incorporates links go from Feature to Epics, not from Feature to individual Tasks.'

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md '## Task Dependency Order' shows: Task 1 (backend model/service) -> Task 2 (backend endpoints) -> Task 3 (backend tests) and Task 4 (frontend API/hooks) -> Task 5 (frontend dashboard) -> Task 6 (frontend table). Backend tasks are numbered 1-3, frontend tasks 4-6. The impact map explicitly states: 'Backend tasks (1-3) have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks (4-6), ensuring correct implementation ordering.'

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Non-doc/non-test tasks (1, 2, 4, 5, 6) all contain: Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Create, Files to Modify, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Task 3 (testing task 'remediation-tests') also contains all sections including Files to Create, Files to Modify, and Implementation Notes. Task 7 (documentation task 'documentation') contains Repository (trustify-backend), Target Branch (main), Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements — exempt sections (Files to Modify/Create, Implementation Notes) are correctly omitted.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md: Epic 1 has '**Issue type:** Epic (level-1)' and '**Parent:** TC-9006 (Feature)'. Epic 2 has '**Issue type:** Epic (level-1)' and '**Parent:** TC-9006 (Feature)'. summary-comment.md Epics Created table confirms 'Issue Type: Epic (level-1)' and 'Parent: TC-9006' for both.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: All 7 task files have a '## Repository' section with exactly one repository name: Tasks 1-3 and 7 have 'trustify-backend'; Tasks 4-6 have 'trustify-ui'. No task contains multiple repository names.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All 7 task files contain: '## Target Branch' (all set to 'main'), '## Description' (all have substantive descriptions), '## Acceptance Criteria' (all have checkbox items), '## Test Requirements' (all have checkbox items).

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All convention enrichments in Implementation Notes follow the prescribed format. Examples from task-1: 'Per CONVENTIONS.md §Module Pattern: follow the model/ + service/ + endpoints/ structure for the remediation module. Applies: task creates `modules/fundamental/src/remediation/model/summary.rs` matching the convention's Rust module file scope.' Task-4: 'Per CONVENTIONS.md §API Layer: Axios client in `src/api/client.ts`... Applies: task modifies `src/api/rest.ts` matching the convention's `.ts` API file scope.' Backend tasks only include Rust-scoped conventions (Module Pattern, Error Handling, Endpoint Registration, Response Types, Caching), frontend tasks only include TypeScript/React-scoped conventions (API Layer, State Management, Naming, Page Structure, Component Library, Routing). No 'Not applicable' annotations appear anywhere. No free-form prose rationales found.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Feature TC-9006 has Priority: Major. impact-map.md '## Inherited Field Values' states: 'Priority: Major (inherited from Feature TC-9006)'. Both Epics include 'priority: {"name": "Major"}' in additional_fields. summary-comment.md states: 'Priority: Major — inherited from Feature TC-9006 and propagated to all tasks and Epics via additional_fields.priority.' The additional_fields JSON block confirms: '"priority": {"name": "Major"}'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Feature TC-9006 has Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0. No '### Jira Field Defaults' section in CLAUDE.md, so fixVersion scope defaults to 'both'. impact-map.md states: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (inherited from Feature TC-9006; no `fixVersion scope` setting in CLAUDE.md, defaulting to "both" — propagated to all tasks)'. Both Epics include 'fixVersions: [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]' in additional_fields. summary-comment.md confirms: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 — inherited from Feature TC-9006. No `fixVersion scope` setting in CLAUDE.md `### Jira Field Defaults`, defaulting to `"both"` — propagated to all tasks and Epics.'

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in the outputs directory and contains a dedicated '## Inherited Field Values' section documenting: 'Priority: Major — inherited from Feature TC-9006 and propagated to all tasks and Epics', 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 — inherited from Feature TC-9006... propagated to all tasks and Epics', 'Labels: ai-generated-jira — applied to all created tasks and Epics'. Additionally, impact-map.md has its own '## Inherited Field Values' section with the same information.
